newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Thursday on market uncertainties with investors continuing to offset their positions in the May 1997 contract due on May 19, traders said.
The most actively-traded May contract ended at 3,305 yuan ($399) per tonne, losing 75 yuan. It opened at 3,365 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,390 and a low of 3,299.
July rose eight yuan to 3,308, September five to 3,318, November fell six 3,382, the January 1998 contract rose two to 3,392 and March fell 10 to 3,380.
Combined volume rose sharply to 39,700 tonnes from 11,200.
Apart from the May contract, other contracts moved in a narrow range for most of the session, traders said.
"Both long and short position holders are eager to offset their positons in the May contract with the approach of the delivery date," one trader said.
Traders said a lack of market-moving news meant soybeans were likely to continue to consolidate in the short term.
